Somerville.narrative: Somerville continues to prove itself as one of Greater Boston's most fiercely competitive markets, with single-family homes commanding a $1,425,000 median sale price and closing at 103% of list — while a remarkable 54.5% of those homes sold above asking price in the last 30 days. Multi-families are the standout asset class, with a $1,580,000 median and nearly two-thirds of sales (66.7%) closing over list at 102.9% SP/LP, reflecting intense investor and owner-occupant demand in a city where rental income potential is sky-high. Condos offer a relatively more accessible entry point at $762,000 median, though even that segment saw 38.5% of units trade above asking at a clean 100% SP/LP ratio across 39 sales. With effectively zero months of supply across all property types, sellers hold enormous leverage and can expect strong offers quickly, while buyers must come prepared with aggressive pricing, clean terms, and the financial flexibility to move fast in a market that simply does not wait.

Cambridge.narrative: Cambridge remains one of the most competitive real estate markets in Greater Boston, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $2,500,000 and selling at 102.2% of list price, while more than half — 52.4% — closed above asking. Condos are equally active, with 72 units sold in the last 30 days at a median of $1,055,500 and half of all sales exceeding list price, and multi-families are following suit at a $2,150,000 median with 42.9% selling over ask. With effectively no months of supply across all property types, inventory is critically tight, leaving buyers facing intense competition and the near-certainty of bidding wars regardless of price point. Sellers, meanwhile, are in an exceptional position — properly priced homes are moving quickly and consistently pulling offers above list, making this an ideal moment to bring a property to market.

Medford.narrative: Medford's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $855,500 and an impressive 61.5% of homes selling above asking price at 101.7% of list price — all against a backdrop of virtually no available inventory. Condos are moving at a median of $790,000 with half of units closing over ask, while multi-families command a striking $1,175,000 median, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant demand for the city's income-producing stock. For sellers, current conditions are about as favorable as it gets — lean supply and persistent buyer competition are consistently driving offers above list price across every segment. Buyers, however, should come prepared with pre-approvals locked, escalation clauses ready, and realistic expectations that waiving contingencies may be necessary to compete in a market where homes are not sitting long enough to accumulate measurable supply.

Melrose.narrative: Melrose's single-family market is running white-hot, with a median sale price of $1,005,000 and homes selling at 106.9% of list price — nearly 70% of the 26 homes sold in the last 30 days closed above asking, a clear signal that buyers are competing aggressively in multiple-offer situations. Condos offer a more measured entry point at a $479,000 median, selling right at list price with only a third going over ask, though the extremely thin inventory across all property types means buyers should expect to move fast and come in strong regardless of segment. Multi-family properties, with just one sale at a $1,075,000 median and a 97.8% SP/LP ratio, are the one area where buyers may have a sliver of negotiating room, though the sample size is too small to draw firm conclusions. For sellers, Melrose is essentially as favorable a market as it gets — price confidently, present well, and the data strongly suggests you'll net above your asking price.

Arlington.narrative: Arlington's single-family market is operating in full seller's-market territory, with a median sale price of $1,370,000 and an average of 105.9% of list price — meaning buyers are routinely writing offers $75,000–$100,000+ above asking, as three out of four homes sold over list price in the past 30 days. Condos are only slightly softer at a $917,000 median and 99.5% SP/LP, though 44% still selling above ask signals genuine competition at that price point as well. Multi-families tell a different story — just 2 sales in 30 days at 94.4% SP/LP with no units going over ask, suggesting investors are pushing back on elevated $1,175,000 median pricing given today's financing costs. Across all segments, the absence of any measurable months of supply means sellers hold the leverage, but buyers who come in pre-approved and aggressive on single-families in particular will need to budget meaningfully above the list price to compete.

Belmont.narrative: Belmont's real estate market is firing on all cylinders, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,975,000 and selling at 103.1% of list price — nearly 89% of homes going above asking — signaling an intensely competitive landscape with virtually no available inventory. Condos are equally aggressive, with a median of $880,000 and 75% of units clearing list price at 103.7% SP/LP, while the multi-family segment tells a contrasting story, with just two sales at a median of $1,019,484 and a 92.9% SP/LP ratio, suggesting buyers have a rare window of negotiating leverage in that product type. For sellers of single-families and condos, conditions couldn't be more favorable — lean supply and strong demand are consistently driving bidding wars and premium pricing. Buyers, however, should come pre-approved, move decisively, and budget well above list price, particularly in the single-family segment where waiving contingencies has become nearly table stakes in this sought-after town.

Watertown.narrative: Watertown's real estate market remains exceptionally tight across all property types, with virtually no measurable months of supply signaling an extreme inventory shortage. The single-family segment is commanding serious attention, with the lone sale in the past 30 days closing at a median of $1,365,000 and 101.1% of list price — though the thin volume makes it difficult to draw broad conclusions. Condos tell a more robust story with 19 sales at a median of $825,000 and 36.8% of units selling above asking price at exactly list price on average, reflecting consistent and competitive demand in that segment. For buyers, expect to move fast, come in at or above asking, and face limited choices; for sellers, this is an opportune moment to list, particularly in the condo and multi-family space where a median multi-family sale of $1,157,000 and 25% of homes selling over ask demonstrate that investor and owner-occupant demand alike remains strong.

Winchester.narrative: Winchester's single-family market is operating at an extraordinary price point, with a median sale of $2,409,000 and homes selling exactly at list price on average — though the real story is that nearly 43% of transactions are closing above ask, signaling fierce competition despite the premium price tier. With effectively no measurable months of supply and 21 homes sold in the past 30 days, inventory is being absorbed as fast as it hits the market. The condo segment is equally aggressive, with a median sale of $703,000, 57% of units selling over list price, and a sale-to-list ratio of 101.9%, meaning buyers are routinely outbidding each other even on attached homes. For sellers, Winchester represents an exceptional opportunity to command top dollar with minimal days on market, while buyers should come prepared with strong pre-approvals, escalation clauses, and the flexibility to waive contingencies to stay competitive.

Boston.narrative: Boston's real estate market remains intensely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a $925,000 median sale price and an extraordinary 103.1% sale-to-list ratio — meaning buyers are routinely paying above asking, as evidenced by nearly 70% of single-family homes selling over list price in the last 30 days. Condos, the most active segment with 371 sales in the past month, are trading at a $825,000 median with a 99% SP/LP ratio, while multi-family properties command a $1,175,000 median and still see 40% of sales closing above asking price. With effectively zero months of supply across all three property types, inventory is critically constrained, giving sellers exceptional leverage and the realistic expectation of multiple offers and strong premiums. For buyers, this market demands pre-approval, aggressive offer strategies, and a willingness to move quickly — there is simply no room to hesitate when homes are selling this fast and this far above list price.
